headline: UBS LIFTS NEWMONT TO $155; HARMONY GOLD SURGES 4% AS SECTOR SHAKES OFF FED HIKE
snippet: UBS raised its Newmont (NYSE: NEM) price target to $155 from $120, reiterating Buy as gold climbed back to $4,324 per ounce on September 17 — one day after the Fed's 25-basis-point hike. Harmony Gold surged 4.0% in pre-market, with Gold Fields +2.3%, AngloGold +2.4%, Agnico Eagle +2.3%, and Kinross +1.2%; the broadening of gains across jurisdictions signals the market has fully absorbed the rate move and is rotating back into gold mining equities.

headline: PERSEVERANCE METALS FINDS EAGLE-ANALOG Ni-Cu BODY IN MICHIGAN, UPSIZES RAISE TO C$10M
snippet: Perseverance Metals (TSXV: PMI) upsized its private placement from C$8M to C$10M on September 17 following a September 9 discovery of a nickel-copper sulphide-bearing mafic-ultramafic intrusion at the Osprey target on the Voyageur Project in Michigan's Upper Peninsula — approximately 65 km west of the Eagle Ni-Cu-PGE mine. Three of four diamond drill holes confirmed the same host-rock type as Eagle; the financing upsize reflects investor demand ahead of aggressive follow-up drilling to vector toward potential massive sulphide-bearing zones.

headline: SILVER STORM'S LA PARRILLA ENTERS GDXJ ON SEPTEMBER 18 — ETF-MANDATED INSTITUTIONAL BUYING NOW BEGINS
snippet: Silver Storm Mining (TSXV: SVRS), operator of the La Parrilla silver-gold mine in Durango, Mexico, enters the MVIS Global Junior Gold Miners Index — the benchmark tracked by the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) — effective at close of trading September 18, 2026, mandating passive index-tracking buying from institutional fund managers. The index requires at least 50% of revenue from gold or silver mining; the company is ramping La Parrilla to steady-state production by Q1 2027 and expects the inclusion to materially improve trading liquidity and institutional visibility.

headline: ICONIC MINERALS HITS GOLD-SILVER IN 5 OF 6 HOLES AT NEVADA CARLIN TREND — SECOND BATCH OF NEW PASS ASSAYS
snippet: Iconic Minerals (TSXV: ICM) released the second batch of 2026 assay results on September 17 from the New Pass gold-silver property in Churchill County, Nevada — five of six drill holes returned continuous near-surface gold-silver mineralization ranging from 30 to 180 feet, with average gold grades of 0.30–0.44 g/t and silver up to 6.49 g/t. The 2,140-hectare property sits along a Carlin-type trend 240 km east of Reno, with the final sample batch now at ALS before initial metallurgical testing confirms heap-leach recoveries.

headline: RPX GOLD DRILLS 35.1M AT 1.87 G/T AU OUTSIDE WAWA PEA PIT — 25 HOLES ADVANCE PFS
snippet: RPX Gold (TSXV: RPX) released assays from 25 holes totalling 4,336 metres at the Wawa Gold Project in Ontario on September 16 — the standout interval returned 1.87 g/t Au over 35.10 m at the southern Jubilee Deposit, including 21.50 g/t Au over 1.0 m, extending gold beyond the 2026 PEA mine plan and confirming open-pit potential to surface in the pit gap; approximately two-thirds of the prefeasibility study drill program is now complete, with a PFS targeted for H1 2027.

headline: GOLDSILVER: 762M OZ ABOVE-GROUND SILVER DRAWN DOWN SINCE 2021 — 'THE HIKE IS PRICED IN, THE POSITIONING ISN'T'
snippet: GoldSilver's post-Fed silver analysis argues that while the 25bp hike was priced at 85–91% probability, CFTC data shows speculative silver longs rebuilt to the 73rd percentile of the past 60 weeks in a falling market — while the physical market runs a 46.3 million ounce 2026 deficit and 762.1 million ounces of above-ground stock have been drawn down since 2021; the piece asks whether $63 silver is generational undervaluation or fair value, hinging on whether real-yield pressure or the structural shortage resolves first.

headline: GDX UP 54% TRAILING YEAR — GOLDSILVER BREAKS DOWN THE OPERATING LEVERAGE MATH FOR GOLD MINERS
snippet: GoldSilver's September analysis explains why GDX posted a 54% trailing one-year return against physical gold's more modest gain: fixed mine costs stay flat while revenue scales proportionally with the gold price, creating operating leverage that multiplies upside during bull runs. The flip side: miners fall faster than bullion in corrections and carry reserve depletion, debt, and equity risks that physical gold never does — making position sizing the critical variable for retail speculators in junior mining names.

headline: GOLD ETFS PULL $9 BILLION IN SEPTEMBER AS GLOBAL HOLDINGS HIT ALL-TIME RECORD 4,189 TONNES
snippet: Gold-backed ETFs have captured $9 billion in fresh capital month-to-date in September, adding to the record $18 billion drawn in August as global holdings climbed to an all-time high of 4,189 tonnes with assets under management hitting $615 billion — up 16%. Morningstar notes GLD captured the largest share of September flows, with Europe narrowly out-buying North America; the scale of institutional demand signals a structural shift in how major asset managers use gold as a permanent portfolio allocation rather than a tactical trade.
